description: Bootstrap Kubernetes the hard way. No scripts.

summary.one_liner: A step-by-step manual tutorial for bootstrapping a basic Kubernetes cluster by hand, with no provisioning scripts, aimed at learning how the components fit together.
summary.what_it_does: The README is a lab-style guide that walks through building a small Kubernetes cluster one task at a time. It covers setting up a jumpbox, provisioning compute resources, creating a certificate authority and TLS certificates, and generating kubeconfig and data encryption config files. It then walks through bootstrapping an etcd cluster, the Kubernetes control plane, and worker nodes, followed by configuring kubectl for remote access, provisioning pod network routes, running a smoke test, and cleaning up. The target layout is one control plane node and two worker nodes, using containerd, CNI, and etcd at the versions listed. The README itself is only the lab index; the individual lab steps are not included in the text provided.
use_cases: learn how Kubernetes components fit together
practice generating TLS certificates for a cluster
study etcd and control plane setup by hand
build a small test cluster on four machines
how_to_run: Read the labs in order: Prerequisites, Setting up the Jumpbox, Provisioning Compute Resources, and onward through Cleaning Up
Provision four ARM64 or AMD64 machines on the same network
Follow each lab's commands to install and configure components manually
notable: No automation scripts: every bootstrap step is done manually to teach the fundamentals
Single control plane node with two worker nodes, sized for learning rather than production
Covers certificate authority, kubeconfig generation, etcd, control plane, workers, and pod network routes in sequence
caveats: Not production ready and may receive only limited community support
Requires four ARM64 or AMD64 machines (virtual or physical) on the same network
Deliberately long manual route, so it is not a quick way to get a working cluster
